answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a bond before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by bonded value and slashes the bond when a challenge proves coordinated fraud, so creating thousands of names does not create thousands of trusted voices. The attacker must lock scarce capital in every identity and risks losing it; a mirror of one agent’s behavior cannot cheaply multiply trust. Even an orchard of accounts rooted in shale must pay that cost.
